notes.title: Happy Halloween - Major Patch 12.0 is now LIVE!
notes.content:
[h2]NEW MAIN FEATURE[/h2]

Destiny Tiling (Texture Randomisation Tiling) is something that is great for making authentic work on clothing such as jeans, dresses, shirts, pants and even
mouse pads, covers or go wild and put it behind you on the green screen! Anything is possible with textures. We love textures and always have, it enriches
our minds with eye candy and a sensation of mysteries and thousands of other different emotive affections. It's style, and we love it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/1c5782c01c6a195b1bb4379affe5df4d7f37c22e.png[/img]

[h2]UPGRADED FEATURE[/h2]

Spray like never before in Shadowforge. Now you can spray directly by pressing on the mouse button instead of only selecting it on the right menu
bar and pressing enter, possibly dividing the spray with a number value. The method of pressing the mouse button, which I introduce as Spray 2.0 for
the app, follows an invisible red thread. As if it has it's own destiny and on it grows new seeds, which in this case is a custom or themed sprite.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/747504f05d0b1593f9030dceb3578d1fec3ecdbc.png[/img]

[h2]REPLACED FEATURE ON THE QUICK BAR WITH A CONSISTENT AND BETTER FEATURE[/h2]

Say good bye to tick tock color value changing and say hello to SCATTER. The SCATTER is divided to Spray 2.0 and Destiny Tiling, but is
a strong foundation pillar.


[h3]NEW SUB FEATURE[/h3]

Meet Scatter Tiling. A sub feature of a foundation feature. It allows you to pick -- with the brush space value input option -- amount of cloned scattered tiles.
Jointed with the Tile Paint Fill, it might be your deal changer for this update.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/2f6b768c49daf8361edad390283c3042cbc3b0d5.png[/img]

[h3]WIDENED USE FOR "W OPTIONS"[/h3]

Now compatible with Spray 2.0 and Texture Randomisation Tiling (but from now on I am going to call it Destiny Tile, because why not, I am 100%
independant and work on this by myself so I can name it what I want. Hehe. But I do take any feedback postively and serious. Anyway, moving on to
the next work that has been scheduled and pushed on...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/2559e55eb8bf2f231e8ba17d59cdb0cee5ac35b0.png[/img]


[h3]BUGS SQUASHED[/h3]
Fixed crash that occured when using the gif upload icon and after that exiting the game.
Now the display is corrected when the preview when you hover on the text for Barrel and Fish distortion is active.


[h3]QOL HEALING[/h3]
The mouse cursor no longer connects with the top camera slider like it used to due to other things taking up Place.

Below image is a character from Bluetail. Having only washed the lightest white into transparency, I decided to try and make a character that was only a quick concept into a portrait painting resembling some kind of oil painting from the 1600's. Keeping the bone structures that were outlined that make this character a personalised design from someone, yet changed into a shaded version with a few textures.

If you are a seasoned Shadowforge painting veteran, you will be right at home in how to do something like this when starting Shadowforge 12.0.

If you're new, read the guide, or TL;DR, ALT + B into CTRL + B into the Red Sphere icon on the Left Quick Bar. Wash a color into transparency with the black and white eraser icon on the Quick Bar.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/b951b156c9087508a9166034893b8e259b14be94.png[/img]

notes.title: Imagination Class #3
notes.content:
[h2]The Bad Monster and the Nice Monster.[/h2]

When you're drawing the evil monster, you have to make it seem like it's a zombie. Just emotionless. No pupils or else he can have feelings like a little puppy. Yellow to red eyes (to not make the viewer feel like it's a ghost). It must have anger, so yellow-red is the way to go. Not a lot of teeth like a shark but it should still look like shark teeth. If you make too many teeth it's basically not humanoid and doesn't "fit in" to the monster you want the character to have an intellectual conflict against.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/91pATzu.png[/img]

Yeah, so what can it be? It doesn't have to be an orc. It can be a bat-like humanoid, a reptile humanoid, or a pesty rat humanoid. Many different animals that we have in the world, and their damage to humans can be made as a bad monster.


So you want to make a nice monster? Then it needs pupils so it can show feelings, eyebrows so that it can show affection, wether it be happy or sad, it shows that it has emotions. Shadows around the eyes does not mean it's an evil workaholic. It's just something to blend in with the eyelashes that makes you memorise the eyes better and it's pretty cool too.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/ZjaIYhc.png[/img]

Whatever you do, don't make it look alien. That might be for another class.

Bon voyage! See you!

notes.title: Imagination Class #1
notes.content:
So you got a great vision of what you want to do but you can't realise it with texture brushes? No problem!

Shadowforge can help you with that. Draw in pixels with the Draw Tiled feature. It's easy to form something out of pixels, and Shadowforge lets you tile them together however big the pixels are. 64x64? Sure! Maybe you can make a face out of it. Well, I did that.

I made a panda face from pixels with bamboo trees in the background and a wooden house that can not be seen because the focus is on the pandas face.

Here is the pixelized version (took me only 5 mins or so): [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/0db61ea62692853600db3367ea81d3ad00f9af81.png[/img]

Then I cartoonized it by not blocking the colors and actually making it cel shaded with simple circle brushes. I wanted the panda to crave for something, and he is making that face when he thinks someone doesn't understand his needs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/7e024c368bb42c2cbd0994e813d696ce954d8cd5.png[/img]

FInally, I used the leaf brush and the alpha brush together to give him some textures to make it look less cartoony but, but still somewhat cartoony.

It should be apparent that the panda has fur, and is not a gummy bear.

Here is the final result of about 15 mins of drawing:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/106d1d8cea91e59102685da021c7940f7a0124d0.png[/img]

notes.title: Why it's perfectly fine to draw with a mouse on Shadowforge
notes.content:
Shadowforge is so easy and user friendly when it comes to drawing with the mouse. Even the developer is drawing with the mouse! That says a lot about it.

Wether you want to change the brush angle with the slider or mathematically type it in, it lets you plan your moves before you rock your grooves, so to speak.

With just pressing on two buttons, ALT+ B, your pen tablet fund is being saved for other things already. ALT + B is color overlay painting. Color overlay painting is when you only paint on what you have already painted. That means that the background that is not painted on, will not be painted on. As simple as that.

You only need 10 layers. Why messing around with 130+ layers is a bad idea: picture a room filled with several thin and single paged paperwork. It's messy, and does not keep you occupied with what you really should be doing. Drawing. Not even grouping them does any wonders.

All you need is to lasso the part you want to modify, then move to another layer, and see it pop up right there so you can edit it. Then you can lasso it again, and move it to the first targeted layer (Shadowforge also supports onion skinning) and you're done. It's way more efficient and time saving then having literally a room that needs to be cleaned.

But enough talk about the layers. What makes Shadowforge work great with mice is also that the AI understands where the outlines should be drawn. So all you have to do is click on Outline, and then press enter. You can hold it down to make it thicker if you want to. Or if you're not satisfied with how the outlines are looking (which is pretty much pixel perfect), then at least you have lines to follow.

You don't need a "pen pressure". You can do more than that. With alpha brush, you can draw until the timer goes off and it says "hey, there's no alpha left" and it depends on how fast you move your mouse.

You also have the scale brush and rotation brush, which is something cool on top of the alpha brush ("mice pressure"). Scale brush can be used for calligraphy, perspective painting, and more. While the rotation brush is very much like a wall painting tool.

There's much more that I have not included in this long post. But hey, if you're a pixel artist that loves using the mouse and wants to move on to other more vibrant colored things, then Shadowforge is for you. Even if you're not a pixel artist, and is a pro-mice only painter, then Shadowforge is a very nice drawing software.

notes.title: How I made one stone floor texture into something else
notes.content:
First of all I want to point out that when you use images from other sources, make sure that it is licensed for free. Use them at your own risk.

Now moving on to how I made Old City Road into this: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/e73a5a9f70d17b43f1e71011581d1ebb285ea166.png[/img]


First of all, you need to make what you want to retexture white. Either by painting it white, or by shading it white. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36815287/e2795dc18e38dd0b0c46951af61a465dac51a3f0.png[/img]

Then you use the Brush Optimizer. Print it on the canvas. Next, upload a single or several images with CTRL + SPACE and then randomize it. You have now successfully changed the texture. But wait, the other stuff (gray stuff?) are now cut out/transparent. Well, use Add Clear Assets and then put in a colored background, then stamp it on the canvas again. Now you're done with your amazing transformation.

notes.title: Shadowforge Forecast Predictions
notes.content:
These are my own predictions for what I will add to Shadowforge when the latest GMS update gets released out of beta. First of all, I want to mention, that none of this might come to existance at all. But the RBS and RBI did release with Shadowforge 3.2, as predicted before. So there might be a chance still.

Lets get the carpet rolling then... What I believe the new GMS update will help greatly with, is it's nine slice feature. I think that this can make it a lot easier to add a 9 vertice tool after you have used a polygon tool, to shape the selected part of your image with scaling and rotation right off the bat. Maybe this is just wishful thinking. I have not tested the beta in fear of losing my project.

Next, I believe I should live up to Shadowforge's name by making light and shadow gradients on selected areas. Remember that this is just my own predictions for the software, I don't want to promise anything because then I'd get angry mobs at me like the angry mmorpg players on youtube, no pun intended.

Some bug fixes here and there. One important thing was that lassoing while outside of the canvas would crash the software (if you're unlucky). That is fixed now.

notes.title: Shadowforge Tips & Tricks
notes.content:
If you are experiencing weird textures when you load your save slot, you will need to delete your files from %localappdata% in the latest Shadowforge folder. Probably only savestate.dat if I'm not mistaken, have not tested it yet. I just deleted them all. But .png files should not interfere with the textures on the UI.

If you hold down CTRL + O you can have your primary brush color on your secondary "background" color as long as you have it held down.

And did you know? Shadowforge has a website and forum. Join the community at www.theshadowforge.com.

If you have not picked a background color, it will make it transparent, so you can still work on a transparent background. Pick transparent or grid background to not make any colors with the lasso tool.

notes.title: Shadowforge 3.0
notes.content:
Added in Lasso Tool. You can access it by pressing ALT + F, remove it by pressing ALT + Q.
When you right click with lasso tool mode on, you can save the lassoed painting to your docker.
Made the lasso tool draw by free hand.

The animation window can get bigger if you right click on it, if you right click on it again it gets back to it's original size.
The docker does not duplicate the animation frames anymore.
When you click on the animation frame on the docker, you'll wipe the drawing you drew and it will get replaced with the drawing on the animation docker.

I made it possible to save all the animation frames you have added on the docker. Just click on the yellow frames on the left UI and pick a folder to save them to.

Some icons have been moved to other places.

Back in 2020, I said that I was going to make a greyscale shader in the future. And here we are, in 2021 and I have kept my word on it. Grey Shader is now live!

The following sprites have been added:

Old Road.
Metal Floor.

Randomize Sprites On Color is a new feature that will only randomize your docked sprites on what you have painted.

If you press ALT + D you can change the right menu into a layer menu where you can view what your layers look like. This is only for the four first layers. I recommend not using the layer menu while drawing on a 4000x4000 or higher canvas. However, you can view the layer menu while not drawing.

Left mouse button pressing on a layer on the menu will take you to that layer.

Made the canvas resize to your input when mouse clicking on the layers. This has been coded on the left and right arrow keys since a long time ago.

Made all layers interactable with all onionskins when clicking on respective layer. This code has been utilized with the left and right arrow keys since a long time ago.

The convex polygon tool (ALT + I) now draws animated stripes around it, instead of just black.

Prevented convex polygon tool from creating an additional polygon from where your cursor were at, when, for example, picking a color.


The pixels in the pixel tool has gotten bigger. Now the cursor shows when you are using the pixel tool. 

Sprites that you have picked will never be drawn on the canvas while using the pixel tool. When you exit it with CTRL + Q, you can continue to draw with sprites.

You can pick your onionskin opacity by hovering over it on the right menu and then writing a number such as 0, 0.1, 0.2 -- all the way to 1. Number 1 is full opacity and number 0 is no opacity. 0.3 shows the onionskin but in a lesser opacity than 0.7.

Press ALT + B to turn on the Color Overlay to paint only on what you have painted.

I also moved the text icon, and I see it as a quality of life fix.

Fixed a crash that occured when you loaded a gif file that had only a few animations.

Resize To Sprite no longer captures the surface. It immediately resizes the sprite you have on your cursor.

Made the sprite on the vertice tool be at it's correct horizontal value. It will not be flipped anymore. The cursor is shown while the vertice tool is up.

Fixed a bug that made drawing on the far left edge not possible.
Fixed when pressing ESC, that the option to choose if you want to exit or not, was being obscured by the animation window.

You can now rename your layers. The onionskins has been increased in quantity to reflect how many layers you can rename.

The cursor is your sprite when you are drawing on the canvas, and no longer the arrow cursor.

Move did nothing and Workshop wasn't really something users used. They have been removed.

Fixed a crash when you used the polygon tool.
Fixed 3D vertices preventing you from using sprites as a mask, you had to draw on the corners. You no longer need to do that. It will mask itself automatically without "outside" help.

Furthermore, I also added one more shape-changing feature to the 3D vert tool, which you can change to and back with ALT + 2 and ALT + 1.

Fixed when you rotate the camera and press on the sliders.

If you pick the unbalanced technique, you start drawing at a minimum size to a maximum size. Well, it describes itself pretty good. It's unbalanced. *smile*

The balanced brush technique inherits the unbalanced brush technique's code, but is gradually increasing in size in perfect harmony.

SF now has a clean graphical UI. Improvements were made to how you interact outside of the Palette and Scale UI when you have pressed on it.

Paint fill is back to what it was, but it makes four grids now instead of one grid. However, painting fast with the paint fill tool on will make you lose some of the grids. I have made the grids represent itself visually while drawing with paint fill mode.

Pressing CTRL + 5 will quickly make your polygons into a triangle. This is appropriate when you want to start making a new polygon tree. For example, you might have made a polygon human hand and after you're done with it and pressed CTRL + T to print it to the surface, then you want to start over to make the arm.

When you press Return, you will not be interacting with the hidden buttons.

Redo is back again! CTRL + R to redo. And the texture won't look weird when you load your custom brushes on "Load project".

When you start Shadowforge again, your undo files are deleted. This makes it a lot easier to focus on your next new project.

Paint filling works with rotating the cam and flipping or mirroring the sprite. I suggest that you use the square brush for paint filling.

I have reduced the amount of lag you get on very big canvases, resulting in the removal of saving back-ups on the docker. Undo is still there, the backend code has just changed to something that is not as laggy in the software client.

I know that gameboy artists like to add a light tint on their art so I made it work with the gameboy shader. Feedback is welcomed, like if there should be white color too or to leave it out and anything else you have in mind.

When you click on load project, the images/brushes you put on the first row will reappear, even if you have exited the app and opened it again.

CTRL + Mouse Wheel to scale your sprite up or down.
SHIFT + Mouse Wheel to zoom the canvas in or out.
CTRL + INSERT key to call in the polygon tool.

You can now eyedrop colors with CTRL + P. The sliders need to be hidden before you do that.
Draw Horizontally and Vertically can be used again.

The fourth row on the docker, which is the images you upload, can now be used with the polygon tool. Must have the sprite on your mouse pointer for it to work.

Using a custom font will no longer change the font on some UI text. Now you can be in text mode as long as you want, if you don't want to be in text mode anymore, press CTRL + Q.

I made some languages fit the UI.

notes.title: Animation Tutorial
notes.content:
Draw parts of your character. Lets draw a bee.

Draw the lower body, the sting, the upper body, the head, left wing and right wing. Make it a sheet.

When you're done, press "F" to copy each part to the "E" docker. You must use the square sprite to copy them. You can scale it. You must also have both the square icon and the "connect points" icon greenlighted. Put the vertices on the canvas, have square sprite icon and vertice icon both greenlighted and then press "F" on a specific part you painted.

You need to select a color from the palette and press "F" until you've cycled the "E" docker. I know it's weird, but that's how it works now.

 Press "T" to move it to the "real" surface, which is the mini canvas. You can also draw on it, it's adviced that you do. When you're done with all body parts, press "F" on them, make a new background or change your canvas size, and then put them on one layer each.

When you've reached the last layer, press "K" to make your sprite invisible. Then...

Press "Y" to begin recording. Press "L" on your keyboard to make them visible, one by one, then press "Y" again to stop the recording and then it prompts you to save the file in gif.

You can also press "Z" or "R".

notes.title: An Open Letter About GMS2

Most GMS2 users are not interested in benefitting the software developers that have spent thousands of hours to help you create something extraordinary. I got 2 down votes on my custom palette tutorial video, and just 1 up vote. Furthermore, I couldn't voice my opinion in the GMS 2.3 development topic about the crippled coding of saving a surface to an image. But I fixed one major bug which was that you could not scale down your image if it's smaller than it's original size. It has been fixed and what I am about to tell you now has nothing to do with a barrier or something I've put on it to get it fixed. 

If you upload an image, it will start with a smaller size than it originally is. However, if you scale it up, it will not lose it's original nice looking textures.

I'm working on fixing the steam workshop. I've seen a lot people trying to upload their brushes. I've now made the images to be stored in the directory path minus directory "Brushes".

A new button has appeared in the software. It's a button you click on to choose if you want to choose all your drawn sprites or just a single one. With it, you can for example scale all individually at once, or just one single image if you switch back to a single drawn sprite.

One interesting feature with that button is that when you pick the "interact with all sprites" button and you choose "Move" on the menu, you can zoom in or out and take a picture of your canvas, it will then be put on your brush, essentially copying the camera border and drawing with it. notes.title: Tip on how to scale
notes.content:
You need to press enter and hold the right mouse button to make the scale work like it should right now. It will be changed later probably. But just so you know how it works now.

Why you get a smaller sized asset on the screen when you scale up and press on the left mouse button: It's supposed to work like this for smaller brushes, so when you draw, it looks prettier. If you want to build game levels or something else by playing with scale and rotate at larger sizes, then you should right click and press on "Add Clear Assets" to "time stop" it to that size.

notes.title: Bugs and the situation right now
notes.content:
There is a bug I can't yet find and I'd also like to add so that you can move, scale and rotate everything in one layer but I currently have no time to do this.

I thought I'd let you know. I don't know when I have time.

notes.title: New Menu UI Design
notes.content: I hope you like it.

notes.title: X and Y independant scaling
notes.content: You can now scale X or Y of the sprite if you have clicked on the Scale Up or Scale Down buttons and then holding down U for horizontal and J for vertical.

notes.title: Drawing in circles is back
notes.content: You just need to hold button Y and left mouse button to do this technique.

notes.title: New sprite rotation on the sprite
notes.content: To solve this, press Enter on the Rotation button.

notes.title: Fixed rotation bug
notes.content: You could somehow get your way through this bug, but if you didn't do it at the start, it prevented you from putting in a value to your rotation. It is now fixed.

notes.title: Here's a few tips for the new patch
notes.content:
If you want the sprite to be visible on your cursor, so that you can get a preview of where you are putting/drawing it on then you must pick a scale for your sprite.

Remember to press on Add Clear Assets if you don't want to scale the previous stamped sprite too.

I've been working all day to make this sprite preview work, and it seems to me that it is working now without any errors.

notes.title: Preview on your cursor of what you're drawing with is now live
notes.content: You can now draw things with the knowledge of where it will be put.

notes.title: Have you decided to make something isometric?
notes.content: Rotate Sprite is now overhauled to not anymore make you draw in circles, Instead now you can input with digits if you hover your mouse over the button and then press enter, and then you can draw with the sprite rotated from the numbers you put in.

notes.title: Menu fix
notes.content: Menu should be working again.

notes.title: How shadowing works in Shadowforge
notes.content: Here's a tip: if you want to be able to upload your images online and make them visible with shadowing, you need to pick a color for your sprite.

notes.title: Fps changed when drawing
notes.content: There should be no holes in the brush stroke anymore.

notes.title: Brush stroke increases very small in size at the start of a stroke
notes.content: If you don't like it, I can revert it back to what it was.

notes.title: Values fixed
notes.content: Color, shadow, alpha and scale values does not any longer scale with how much you draw on layers. This was an unintentional bug.

notes.title: Shadowforge now has 100 layers
notes.content: Shadowforge has been updated now with more layers, in total 100 for painting but animating still has the same amount of layers.

notes.title: Millions of new color options for Pro users
notes.content: Shadowforge now features custom picking of saturation for pro users. This opens up millions of new colors. Press X and C to tune the saturation down or up.

notes.title: Removal of button G, instead pick where you want your frame to end
notes.content: Pick the frame to end at by pressing button I, play the animation by pressing button P, wait and save the animation (if you have pro).

notes.title: Animation update
notes.content:
For free and pro users:
Press P to play the animation.

[h3]For Pro users:[/h3]
Press G to record the animation, and when it ends, press G again to save it on file.

notes.title: Button highlight and permanent underwater fx fix
notes.content: When you press enter the button is highlighted green. If you press on Add Clear Assets, the underwater effect disappears, but you can make it appear again if you press on it's button again.

notes.title: New canvas tip
notes.content: It's a small update, but I thought I'd let you know that you only need to hover over the two buttons and input a size and then only press enter (not with enter and mouse anymore).

notes.title: Canvas Resize Bug Cleaned
notes.content: You should now be able to resize your canvas the appropriate way.

notes.title: Mini Canvas
notes.content: If you press M you can show/hide the mini canvas.

notes.title: How to get around Erase Tool totally blackholing everything
notes.content: Press button F to make the erase tool essentially a visible drawing tool, then press the Z button to undo the erase tool.

notes.title: Animation
notes.content:
By pressing Q and W you change the animation layers. This is an update for all Shadowforge users. Press "K" to turn the layer invisible and press "L" to make it 100% visible.

You can't save them as a gif animation clip, but you can save them individually and then use another software or website to animate the images.

And here's a tip: You can save to many image formats if you write ".jpg, .gif, .png, .jpeg, etc.".

notes.title: Shadowforge Pro users can now resize their canvas
notes.content:
Thank you Pro users for making this happen. Press Left Mouse Button + Enter when you hover over the canvas resize button to resize your canvas. Before you do all that don't forget to write in the numbers on your keyboard and then press enter!

Best regards,
Mibli.

notes.title: Workshop Integration with Shadowforge
notes.content:
Hello all Shadowforgers or to-be Shadowforgers!

The workshop integration is done and should work on launch. Remember that it is a community driven effort that makes the art stand out. And how can you help out? By making your own brushes and sharing it. With only one pressed button, it will instantly show up in the workshop. However, you will need to make a folder named "Brushes" in your steamapp Shadowforge folder,  and then you can upload all your wonderful brushes but they must have a title, description and an image!

Start forging your pencil, because the pencil is stronger than a sword!

Best regards,
Mibli.
